summary.answer: Connected the existing post-armor damage payload to two different channels: threaded on_player_damage table listeners observe the victim and can record damage to a reviver on its revivee's stats, while laststand_damage is an entity notify consumed by the already-downed bleedout listener. That listener uses the pre-local-substitution payload damage and selected tier health/time. Local idamage=1, self.health++ and self.laststanddamage follow notification; they do not explicitly rewrite params. The later damage gate can return after these side effects. Revive marker/clears and cancellation paths are mapped without claiming listener ordering, native delivery, parameter alias rules or real PS4 behavior.
unknowns: Exact parameter object alias/copy rules across native eventstruct -> callback locals -> params -> threaded table listeners -> entity notify payload are unproved. The source reuses one params variable and does not write params.idamage=1; this does not prove immutable/deep-copy payloads or forbid a shared listener mutation.

Only the bounded WZ on_player_damage consumer was inspected for writes: it reads params and writes revivee telemetry. Other loaded/hashed subscribers, callback-table mutations and native field aliases can change observations; no global absence or immutable payload claim is made.

Thread spawn/run interleave and live-state read timing are unresolved: WZ reviver comparison uses self.health, producer checks self.laststand after table dispatch, and revive window/health writes can overlap. No callbacks finish-before-notify assumption is used.

Native notify delivery/queueing and endon/endoncallback cancellation semantics, especially combined keys and a notification during the initial wait, remain standing g3 A.4/f2 N4/b2 conditions. Source notification is not delivery proof.
